summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and a history of recurrent cellulitis was admitted for worsening bilateral leg swelling and concern for cellulitis. She was treated empirically with a five-day course of IV vancomycin, though infection was unlikely due to absence of fever and minimal leukocytosis. Imaging ruled out deep vein thrombosis, and right heart catheterization showed borderline elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure with normal cardiac output, indicating that heart failure was not the primary cause of edema. Her fluid overload was managed with IV furosemide and transitioned to oral bumetanide. Kidney function transiently worsened, likely due to diuretics, prompting temporary dose reductions in her seizure medications. The lymphedema team initiated compression wrapping, and she was discharged to a rehab facility for ongoing management. Pain control was maintained on her baseline opioid regimen, warfarin was continued for prior DVT/PE, and penicillin prophylaxis was discontinued per infectious disease. She left with stable vital signs, improved edema, and a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
